overall_summary: Bitcoin faces a clearly risk-off tape today. Persistent ETF outflows, miner selling, shrinking stablecoin supply, and a hawkish inflation-driven rates repricing are stacking pressure, while dollar strength and higher yields add macro headwinds. Geopolitics is mixed with some peace-talk optimism, but it is not enough to offset the crypto-specific and rates drag.
key_points: Fifth day of Bitcoin ETF outflows, ~$300M exit
Hot CPI drives hawkish Fed, yields and dollar up
MARA dumps $1.1B BTC; miner selling pressure
Peace-talk hopes offset by Hormuz and Iran risks

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs See Fifth Day of Outflows, $300M Exit
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded another $299.9 million in net outflows on Wednesday, marking a fifth straight day of redemptions and roughly $1.44 billion since early November. BlackRock’s IBIT drove most of it with nearly $270 million leaving. Traders should care because sustained ETF selling removes a key source of institutional demand and has kept Bitcoin hovering near $73,400 amid broader risk-off pressure.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure and weaker spot demand near current levels

items.title: Nvidia CEO Turmoil Hits Tech Stocks and Bitcoin
items.summary: Reports that Nvidia’s board may oust CEO Jensen Huang sent the stock down around 7 percent pre-market and pulled Nasdaq futures lower. Bitcoin slipped about 0.7 percent in sympathy as risk appetite faded across tech-linked assets. Crypto traders need to watch this because Bitcoin has been trading in lockstep with AI and mega-cap tech; further Nvidia weakness could keep pressure on BTC until the situation clarifies.
items.impact: Risk-off spillover weighing on Bitcoin near support

items.title: MSCI Drops Strategy From Indexes Over Bitcoin Holdings
items.summary: Index provider MSCI will remove Strategy, the largest corporate Bitcoin holder with over 850,000 BTC, from its USA and global indexes effective November 30 under new non-operating company rules. Passive funds tracking those indexes will have to sell shares, with estimates of initial outflows around $2.8 billion. This matters because it could pressure Strategy’s ability to raise capital for more Bitcoin buys and signals index providers treating pure treasury plays differently.
items.impact: Potential forced selling of MSTR shares and slower corporate BTC accumulation

items.title: Stablecoin Supply Contracts $14.2B, Fastest Since 2022
items.summary: Glassnode data shows total stablecoin supply fell $14.2 billion over the past 30 days, the steepest drop since the 2022 bear market, with USDT and USDC leading redemptions. The pool now sits near multi-month lows around $280-290 billion. Traders should care because shrinking stablecoin supply means less dry powder sitting ready to buy dips, leaving Bitcoin more vulnerable to any further outflows or macro shocks.
items.impact: Thinner liquidity and reduced buying power for any rebound

items.title: MARA Sells $1.1 Billion in Bitcoin After Quarter-End
items.summary: Mining giant MARA Holdings sold 13,597 BTC for about $1.1 billion after September 30 at an average near $81,000, using $750 million to repay bitcoin-backed loans and free collateral. The firm said it plans more sales to fund AI infrastructure, debt and buybacks. This is relevant because large miner sales add supply to the market at a time when ETF demand is already weak and public companies have sold over 100,000 BTC this year.
items.impact: Additional spot supply pressure from a major holder

items.title: Bitcoin Core Discloses High-Severity Mining Node Bug
items.summary: Bitcoin Core published details of three previously patched vulnerabilities, including a high-severity issue that could leave a mining node unable to build valid block templates after a chain reorg until restarted. The flaws were fixed in October 2025 releases and disclosed now after older versions reached end of support; no exploits were reported. Node operators and miners should update if still on affected versions, but the market impact is limited since the issues are already resolved.
items.impact: Short-term FUD possible but no active threat after patches

items.title: Hot October CPI Sparks Hawkish Fed Repricing
items.summary: October CPI came in hotter than expected at 0.4 percent month-over-month headline and 0.3 percent core, the third straight firm core print. Fed Governor Waller had flagged a possible 50 basis point hike if core hit that level, and markets fully priced a December hike with rising odds of a larger move. Traders should care because this keeps the Fed on a tightening path into year-end, raising the discount rate on risk assets and pressuring liquidity conditions that crypto thrives on.
items.impact: Higher rate path weighs on Bitcoin and equities

items.title: Dollar Hits 19-Month High on Rate Divergence
items.summary: The DXY dollar index surged to around 103, its highest since April 2025, after the CPI surprise and hawkish Fed comments. Two-year yield spreads widened versus Europe and Japan as markets bet the US can handle higher rates longer. Crypto traders watch this closely because a strong dollar typically pressures Bitcoin as a risk asset and drains global dollar liquidity.
items.impact: Stronger DXY headwind for crypto prices

items.title: Treasury Yields Jump, 2-Year Biggest Rise in Months
items.summary: Short-term Treasury yields surged after the inflation data, with the two-year up about 17 to 19 basis points to around 4.73 percent, the largest daily move since the April 2025 tariff shock. The 10-year climbed near 4.99 percent. This matters for traders because higher yields raise borrowing costs and compete with non-yielding assets like Bitcoin, often triggering risk-off flows.

items.title: Goldman Adds March Hike After Hot Inflation
items.summary: Goldman Sachs revised its Fed outlook to include a 25 basis point hike in March 2027 on top of December, citing the third straight upside inflation surprise and sticky start-of-year pressures. They pushed rate cuts back to late 2027. This reinforces the higher-for-longer narrative that crypto traders must price in for funding and valuation models.

items.title: Jobless Claims and Home Sales Due Today
items.summary: Weekly initial jobless claims print this morning with consensus near 195 thousand after last week's low 189 thousand reading, alongside October existing home sales expected around 3.85 million. A soft claims number would reinforce the tight labor market that supports further Fed hikes. These are the key scheduled US data today and can swing rate expectations and the dollar ahead of PPI tomorrow.
items.impact: Data could confirm or challenge hike pricing

items.title: Fed Speakers Today; PPI Tomorrow Key Test
items.summary: New York Fed President Williams, Governor Barr, and Cleveland Fed's Hammack speak today, with markets listening for any 50 basis point signals after Waller's comments. October PPI is due Friday morning and will show if producer price pressures are still building. Crypto desks should monitor because any further hawkish tilt or hot PPI keeps the December hike fully locked and risk assets under pressure.
items.impact: Speeches and PPI set near-term rate path tone

items.title: IRGC: Two Supertankers Disabled by Explosions in Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil supertankers were hit by massive explosions overnight after taking an unauthorized southern route through the Strait of Hormuz, leaving them disabled. Iranian media later claimed the ships struck naval mines and together carried more than four million barrels of oil. The US had said the waterway's mines were cleared. Traders should watch this closely because any fresh disruption to the key chokepoint keeps oil supply risk elevated and can quickly spill into broader risk-off moves across markets including crypto.
items.impact: Higher oil volatility and risk-off pressure on risk assets

items.title: Kushner and Witkoff Arrive in Moscow for Putin Talks
items.summary: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff landed in Moscow Thursday morning and were met by Putin's envoy ahead of talks with the Russian president. This follows two days of US-mediated negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia and Ukraine that produced a large-scale prisoner exchange deal but no breakthrough on territory or a ceasefire. The pair plan to head to Dublin afterward to brief Zelenskyy and push for Europeans to join future talks. Any real progress here would ease a major geopolitical overhang and support risk assets.
items.impact: De-escalation hopes supportive for risk appetite and crypto

items.title: Abu Dhabi Talks Yield Major Ukraine-Russia Prisoner Swap
items.summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed in principle to their biggest prisoner exchange of the war after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, the first direct US-mediated round in nine months. Numbers are still being finalized, with figures of around one thousand or more per side discussed, but deep differences remain on land and security guarantees. Kushner called it a positive first step while both sides noted tough discussions. Humanitarian progress without a ceasefire keeps the conflict in focus but shows diplomacy is moving again.
items.impact: Limited immediate market move pending territorial progress

items.title: Oil Slips on Iran and Ukraine Peace Hopes
items.summary: Brent crude fell more than a dollar toward the low nineties on Thursday as markets priced hopes for progress on both the Iran conflict and Russia-Ukraine talks. Traders noted behind-the-scenes efforts and reduced odds of immediate major new strikes even as Hormuz risks linger. OPEC-plus output rose in October. Softening energy prices can ease inflation pressure and support broader risk sentiment if the de-escalation narrative holds.
items.impact: Lower oil supports risk-on conditions for equities and crypto

items.title: Israel Security Cabinet to Meet Amid Iran Strike Prep
items.summary: Israel's security cabinet is set to convene Sunday for the first time since early October after reports it ordered the IDF to raise readiness for possible strikes on Iran. Opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot warned Netanyahu against major military moves while the caretaker government lacks full Knesset confidence. This comes as the US signals less need for large new combat operations. Fresh escalation risk between Israel and Iran remains a key wildcard for oil and global risk markets.
items.impact: Escalation risk could reverse oil declines and hit risk assets

items.title: EU Envoys Agree 145 New Russia Sanctions Listings
items.summary: EU ambassadors agreed Wednesday to add one hundred forty-five individuals and entities to Russia sanctions lists, including about fifty banks plus shadow fleet enablers, energy firms and hybrid warfare actors. Foreign ministers are expected to rubber-stamp the package on Monday. The move targets financial networks and oil circumvention while talks with Moscow continue. Fresh sanctions keep pressure on Russian energy flows and complicate any rapid normalization of European risk.
items.impact: Incremental pressure on Russian energy and compliance costs
